intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day speedboat tour around the stunning Phi Phi archipelago, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Viking Cave, and swimming at Monkey Beach. Includes snorkeling gear, lunch, and hotel transfers from Krabi or Phuket.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Beachfront Street Food Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant beachfront night market along Klong Dao Beach, sampling authentic Thai street food including pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, fresh seafood, and local coconut ice cream. Interact with local vendors and discover hidden food stalls along the shore.

experiences.name: Similan Islands Liveaboard Diving & Snorkeling
experiences.description: Join an overnight liveaboard trip to the world-renowned Similan Islands, one of Thailand's top dive sites. Snorkel or dive among vibrant coral reefs, sea turtles, reef sharks, and manta rays. Includes meals, equipment rental, and guided dives across multiple pristine sites.

experiences.name: Koh Samui Beachfront Thai Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Thai cooking class set steps from the beach in Chaweng. Learn to prepare classic dishes like green curry, tom yum soup, and papaya salad using fresh ingredients from a local morning market visit. Enjoy your creations for lunch with ocean views.

experiences.name: Railay Beach Rock Climbing & Sunset Kayaking
experiences.description: Spend a day at the breathtaking Railay Peninsula, accessible only by longtail boat. Take a guided beginner rock climbing session on the iconic limestone karsts in the morning, then kayak through sea caves and hidden lagoons as the sun sets over the Andaman Sea.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Phuket/Krabi Airport, clear customs, and take a shared minivan or bus to the pier. Board the afternoon ferry to Phi Phi Islands (Don). Check into your boutique guesthouse, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront promenade to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tonsai Village on foot — browse the lively night market stalls, watch fire shows on the beach, and soak in the laid-back island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport — pad kra pao rice box from a airport food court stall (~100 THB)
meals.lunch: Eat on the ferry or grab a quick bite at Tonsai Pier — mango sticky rice or grilled corn from street vendors (~60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Night Market — try pad thai, som tum, and grilled skewers from street stalls (~150–200 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance or at the pier (approx. 350–500 THB). Shared minivan from airport is cheapest option (~150–200 THB). Arrive at pier by 15:00 to catch the late afternoon ferry.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and hike up to Phi Phi Viewpoint — a 20-minute steep climb rewarded with a breathtaking panoramic view of both bays. Best done before 9:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds. Entry fee is minimal (~30 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Long Beach (Haad Yao) by longtail boat (~50 THB) for a relaxed afternoon of swimming and snorkeling in crystal-clear water. Rent basic snorkel gear from local shops (~100 THB/hour). The beach is less crowded than Tonsai.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and join a communal beach bonfire gathering. Walk the main strip and enjoy cheap Chang beers from 7-Eleven while watching the sunset from the pier.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near the guesthouse — banana roti with condensed milk and a Thai iced coffee (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside food shack at Long Beach — fried rice with egg or chicken (~100–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Papaya restaurant in Tonsai Village — green curry with jasmine rice (~120 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Start the viewpoint hike no later than 7:30 AM to avoid midday heat. Wear sturdy sandals or shoes. Bring 1–2 liters of water. October may bring brief afternoon rain showers — carry a small poncho.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling day trip departing from Tonsai Pier (~500–700 THB including equipment). Visit Maya Bay (the famous 'The Beach' filming location), Pileh Lagoon, and Monkey Beach. Boats typically depart at 8:30 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island hopping tour — swim through the emerald green Pileh Lagoon, spot monkeys at Monkey Beach, and snorkel at Shark Point where you may see harmless blacktip reef sharks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by 17:00. Rinse off and wander to the quieter northern end of Loh Dalum Bay to watch the sunset with a cold coconut in hand.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast if included, or a nearby stall — khao tom (rice porridge) with egg (~60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch typically included in the tour, or buy grilled fish on a stick at the pier (~50–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Cosmic Restaurant or similar beachfront eatery — massaman curry and rice (~130–150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book the group snorkeling tour the evening before to secure a spot. Avoid private longtail tours which cost significantly more. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Maya Bay has restricted visitor numbers — confirm tour operator compliance.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hours, ~300 THB). Check into a budget guesthouse near Chao Fa Pier. Drop your bags and explore Krabi Town's colorful walking street and iconic Viking Cave murals at the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram — a stunning white temple on a hill offering great views over Krabi Town (free entry). Then explore the Krabi Town Weekend Market stalls even if goods are limited on a weekday — the surrounding area has great local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the famous Krabi Town Night Market (Thanon Khong Kha walking street) for the best and cheapest street food on the trip.

meals.breakfast: On the ferry — buy packaged snacks, or eat before boarding at Tonsai (~60 THB)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Chao Fa Pier — boat noodles or khao man gai (poached chicken rice) (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town Night Market — sample multiple dishes: spring rolls, pad see ew, fresh coconut ice cream (~150–200 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedule from Phi Phi to Krabi typically departs at 9:00 AM and 13:00 PM. Book accommodation in Krabi Town near the pier for easy access to onward transport. Budget guesthouses run 300–500 THB/night.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat tour to the famous Four Islands (Koh Mor, Koh Chueak, Koh Tub, Koh Kai) departing from Krabi Town pier (~500–600 THB group tour). Snorkel at Koh Chueak's vibrant coral reef and walk the sandbar at low tide connecting Koh Tub and Koh Mor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Chicken Island (Koh Kai) — named for its rock formation resembling a chicken head. Snorkel the shallow reef and relax on the white sand beach. Return to Krabi by 16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Krabi's Chao Fa Pier at sunset for golden hour photos of the limestone karsts rising from the Andaman Sea. Stroll along the riverside promenade.

meals.breakfast: Street cart near guesthouse — khanom krok (coconut pancakes) and Thai iced tea (~60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by tour, or fresh fruit and grilled seafood from a beach vendor on the islands (~100 THB)
meals.dinner: May and Mark Restaurant (local favorite) — tom yum soup and stir-fried morning glory (~150–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: October is shoulder season — water visibility may vary but tours still operate. Confirm tour departure the evening before. Bring cash as island vendors rarely accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike or join a shared songthaew to Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for a stunning 360-degree view of Krabi's jungle and karst landscape. Arrive early to beat the heat (~30 THB entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and take a songthaew to Ao Nang Beach (~50 THB). Walk the beachfront strip, browse souvenir shops, and dip in the sea. Ao Nang is busier and more commercial but worth a visit.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Ao Nang's lively beach strip at night — fire shows, beachside bars, and street food carts line the promenade. Take the last songthaew back to Krabi Town (~50 THB).

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse or nearby stall — jok (rice congee) with pork (~70 THB)
meals.lunch: Ao Nang beachfront food court — pad thai with shrimp (~120 THB)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang street food stalls — grilled squid, mango salad, and fresh coconut (~160–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Tiger Cave Temple climb is intense — bring lots of water, wear light clothing, and avoid midday heat. Monkeys near the base may grab bags — keep belongings secure. Motorbike rental is ~200–300 THB/day if you have a license.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a shared minivan or bus from Krabi to Koh Lanta (~200–250 THB, approx. 2 hours including ferry crossings). Check into a budget bungalow on Klong Dao Beach — the island's most accessible and family-friendly beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~80–100 THB/day) and cycle south along the west coast road, stopping at Long Beach (Klong Nin) for a swim. The road passes through jungle and offers stunning sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the slower pace of Koh Lanta. Watch the sunset from the beach with a beer from a local shop. The island is known for its relaxed, non-commercialized vibe.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing Krabi — rice with egg from a street cart (~60 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant on Klong Dao — fried rice with vegetables (~100–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near bungalow — fresh grilled fish with steamed rice and papaya salad (~180–220 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is quieter than Phi Phi and Krabi — ideal for a mid-trip rest day. Budget bungalows on the beach run 400–700 THB/night. Confirm minivan pickup from your Krabi guesthouse the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) by bicycle or motorbike — a charming sea-gypsy fishing village with colorful wooden shophouses on stilts over the water. Visit the small local market and old Chinese temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island (~200 THB entry). Hike to the lighthouse for panoramic views, explore jungle trails, and spot wildlife including monitor lizards and hornbills.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Klong Dao or Klong Nin beach for sunset. Join other travelers at a beachside bar for happy hour (buy-one-get-one cocktails are common, ~100–150 THB each).

meals.breakfast: Old Town morning market — fresh fruit, sticky rice with mango, and Thai coffee (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Picnic from Old Town market or national park entrance food stall — grilled chicken skewers and sticky rice (~100 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant — red curry with coconut milk and jasmine rice (~140 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Old Town is best visited in the morning when the market is active. The national park road is rough — motorbike recommended over bicycle for this trip. Bring insect repellent for jungle trails.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget snorkeling day trip from Koh Lanta to the Trang Islands — including Koh Rok (known for its stunning turquoise water and vibrant coral) and Koh Ha (~700–900 THB including equipment and lunch).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at Koh Ha's underwater caves and pinnacles — one of the best snorkeling spots in the Andaman. The water clarity here is exceptional even in October.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by 17:00. Pack your bags for tomorrow's travel. Enjoy a final relaxing evening on Klong Dao Beach.

meals.breakfast: Bungalow breakfast if included, or fruit smoothie and toast from a beachside café (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in tour — typically simple Thai rice dishes served on the boat or beach
meals.dinner: Night market near Klong Dao — tom kha gai soup, spring rolls, and fresh fruit shake (~170 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is a national marine park — no plastic, no touching coral. Book the tour the day before. October water conditions are generally good for snorkeling in this area despite being shoulder season.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the ferry and minivan combination from Koh Lanta back toward the Andaman coast, heading to Koh Ngai (Koh Hai) — a tiny, pristine island with no cars, perfect for a secluded beach experience (~400–500 THB total travel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Ngai and check into a budget bungalow. The island has a small number of resorts — budget options exist near the pier. Spend the afternoon snorkeling directly off the beach — the house reef is excellent.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sun dip behind Koh Mook and Koh Kradan on the horizon. Dine at your resort or the only small restaurant on the island. Enjoy the stars — there's minimal light pollution here.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing Koh Lanta — roti with banana and honey from a street stall (~60 THB)
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry — packaged food or fresh fruit (~80 THB)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant (limited options on the island) — grilled barracuda with rice and vegetables (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Ngai is one of the most peaceful islands in the region. Budget accommodation is limited — book ahead. Bring enough cash as there are no ATMs on the island. Electricity may be limited to certain hours.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at sunrise and snorkel the house reef before other guests are awake — the water is glassy and fish activity is highest in early morning. Look for clownfish, parrotfish, and sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat to Koh Mook (~100 THB) to visit the famous Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot) — swim through a dark 80-meter tunnel to emerge in a hidden lagoon with towering limestone walls. Go at low tide for best access.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Ngai for a final peaceful evening. Collect shells on the beach, read a book in a hammock, and enjoy the simplicity of island life.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fruit plate, toast, and instant coffee (~100–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Beach shack on Koh Mook — fried rice with egg and cold Singha beer (~130 THB)
meals.dinner: Resort dinner — yellow curry with tofu or chicken (~180–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Emerald Cave is best visited at low tide — check tide times the night before. The swim through the cave is about 80 meters in complete darkness — follow your guide closely. Not recommended for non-swimmers.

day_by_day.morning: Final island morning — take one last swim and snorkel at Koh Ngai's beach. Pack up and take the morning ferry back toward the mainland (Pak Meng or Trang pier). Connect via shared minivan to Trang town (~200 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Trang Town — a charming, non-touristy southern Thai city known for its incredible food culture. Visit the Trang Clock Tower, the old Sino-Portuguese shophouses on Praram 6 Road, and the bustling daytime market.
day_by_day.evening: Trang's dim sum and roast pork culture is legendary in southern Thailand. Spend the evening eating your way through the town's famous coffee shops and street food scene.

meals.breakfast: Last breakfast on Koh Ngai — simple toast and fruit (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Trang market — khao yam (southern Thai rice salad) and fresh coconut water (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Trang's famous Kow Tom Pla (fish rice porridge) at a local coffee shop, plus moo yang (grilled pork) (~150–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Trang is an underrated food destination — don't miss the local dim sum (tiim sum) which is unique to this region. Budget guesthouses in Trang town run 300–450 THB/night. From here, easy onward transport to Bangkok or Phuket airport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Trang — visit the famous Trang Morning Market for a quintessential southern Thai breakfast experience. Try khanom jeen (fermented rice noodles with curry) and fresh tropical fruits like rambutan and langsat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight: take a shared minivan or bus to Trang Airport, or connect to Krabi/Phuket Airport for international departures (~200–350 THB). Allow ample time for travel. Do last-minute souvenir shopping at the market — dried seafood, local coffee, and Thai snacks make great gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Thailand with a full stomach, a sun-kissed glow, and memories of turquoise waters, limestone karsts, and incredible street food. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Trang Morning Market — khanom jeen with fish curry and fresh fruit (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store snacks before departure (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure for airport transfers from Trang. Trang Airport has limited flights — Krabi or Phuket airports offer more international connections. Exchange remaining Thai Baht before departure or at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and take a shared minivan or taxi to Rassada Pier in Phuket, then board a high-speed ferry to Phi Phi Don Island (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the Ton Sai Village beachfront to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Ton Sai Village night market. Browse local stalls, soak in the island atmosphere, and enjoy your first evening on Phi Phi.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: Light meal or snacks at the pier or on the ferry
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant on Ton Sai — mid-range Thai dishes including pad thai, green curry, and fresh seafood; approx. 200–350 THB per dish

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance during October as it can be busy. Keep your luggage light and manageable for the ferry boarding. October is late rainy season — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–45 min uphill walk). Enjoy stunning panoramic views of both Ton Sai Bay and Loh Dalum Bay at sunrise. Return to hotel for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling longtail boat trip around Phi Phi Don — visit Monkey Beach, Shark Point, and the coral reefs near Phi Phi Leh. Spot blacktip reef sharks, colorful fish, and vibrant coral. Book through your hotel or a local operator (approx. 600–900 THB per person).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Loh Dalum Bay beach for sunset views. Relax on the beach before dinner. Browse the beachfront bars for a casual drink.

meals.breakfast: Baan Kosta Restaurant — fresh fruit, eggs, and toast with coffee; approx. 150–200 THB
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch from a nearby street stall before the boat trip — mango sticky rice and grilled corn
meals.dinner: Unni's Restaurant — beloved local spot serving authentic Thai curries and seafood; approx. 200–400 THB per dish

day_by_day.notes: Wear reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Bring cash as many boat operators don't accept cards. The viewpoint hike can be slippery after rain — wear good shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island hopping tour to Phi Phi Leh — visit the famous Maya Bay (where 'The Beach' was filmed), Pileh Lagoon (emerald green enclosed lagoon), and Viking Cave. Swim and snorkel in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island hopping tour with stops at Bamboo Island for beach relaxation and snorkeling over shallow coral gardens. Enjoy a packed lunch on the boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Shower and rest. Head out for a relaxed evening walk through Ton Sai Village and enjoy street food from the night stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — rice porridge (jok) with egg from a street stall; approx. 60–80 THB
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included with most full-day island hopping tours, or buy from a beachside vendor on Bamboo Island
meals.dinner: Phi Phi Street Food Alley — try grilled satay skewers, pad kra pao (basil stir-fry), and fresh coconut; approx. 150–250 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted access with timed entry — ensure your tour operator has the proper permits. Book the full-day tour at least one day in advance. Bring waterproof bags for your belongings.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak (approx. 150–200 THB/hour) and explore the coastline of Phi Phi Don independently. Paddle to hidden coves and small beaches inaccessible by foot. Great for photography and peaceful exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat to Loh Moo Dee Bay or Laem Thong Beach (northern tip of Phi Phi Don) — quieter, more secluded beaches perfect for swimming and sunbathing. Enjoy the calmer atmosphere away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Thai fire show on Loh Dalum Beach (free to watch from the beach). Many beach bars host these nightly. Enjoy cocktails at a beachfront bar.

meals.breakfast: Cosmic Restaurant — popular breakfast spot with smoothie bowls, pancakes, and Thai omelets; approx. 150–250 THB
meals.lunch: Beachside food vendor at Laem Thong — fresh grilled fish and sticky rice; approx. 120–180 THB
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant near Ton Sai pier — tom yum soup, massaman curry, and jasmine rice; approx. 200–350 THB

day_by_day.notes: Laem Thong Beach is a longer longtail ride (approx. 20–30 min) — negotiate the price beforehand (approx. 300–500 THB round trip). Carry drinking water as facilities are limited on northern beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands by morning ferry to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hours). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Krabi Town. Walk along the scenic Krabi riverside promenade and visit the quirky giant crab statue — a local landmark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram — a beautiful white Buddhist temple in the center of Krabi Town with golden Buddha statues and ornate architecture. Then explore the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Sua) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking views over Krabi (allow 1.5–2 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the famous Krabi Town Night Market (open Thursday–Sunday) or the weekend Walking Street for incredible street food. If not a weekend, explore the Chao Fa Night Market along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Light snack on the ferry — buy from the ferry snack vendor
meals.lunch: May and Mark's Kitchen in Krabi Town — famous for authentic Southern Thai cuisine; try the massaman and yellow curry; approx. 150–300 THB
meals.dinner: Krabi Night Market — sample pad thai, grilled seafood, mango sticky rice, and fresh fruit juices; budget 150–250 THB for a full street food spread

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes and carry water. Modest dress required for temple visits (cover shoulders and knees). Krabi Town is a great base for exploring the mainland.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Four Islands Tour departing from Krabi — visit Koh Lading (snorkeling), Koh Mook (Emerald Cave — swim through a dark tunnel to a hidden inland beach), Koh Ngai (stunning turquoise waters), and Koh Kradan (pristine white sand). Tour departs around 8:30 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands Tour. Enjoy swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing on the beautiful beaches of Koh Ngai and Koh Kradan. Packed lunch is typically included.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by late afternoon. Rest and freshen up. Explore the riverside cafés and enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a roti with banana and condensed milk from a street vendor; approx. 50–80 THB
meals.lunch: Included in Four Islands Tour package (typically a Thai lunch box on one of the islands)
meals.dinner: Gecko Cabane — riverside restaurant in Krabi Town with a mix of Thai and Western dishes; approx. 200–400 THB

day_by_day.notes: Book the Four Islands Tour through your guesthouse or a reputable local operator (approx. 800–1,200 THB per person). The Emerald Cave visit requires swimming through a dark 80-meter tunnel — bring a small waterproof flashlight if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Krabi to Railay Beach (15–20 min, approx. 100–150 THB one way) — this stunning beach is only accessible by boat due to surrounding limestone cliffs. Explore Railay West Beach and Railay East Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to Phra Nang Cave (Princess Cave) — a sacred cave shrine on the beach filled with colorful offerings. Then hike the jungle trail to the Railay Viewpoint for panoramic views. Optional: try rock climbing on the famous limestone cliffs (beginner courses available from approx. 1,000–1,500 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Railay West Beach — one of the most photogenic sunsets in Thailand. Return to Krabi by longtail boat. Enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Krabi Town café — fresh fruit smoothie and khao tom (rice soup); approx. 100–150 THB
meals.lunch: Railay Beach restaurant — fresh seafood platter or green papaya salad; approx. 200–350 THB (slightly higher prices due to location)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang street food area (take a short songthaew from Krabi) — grilled prawns, som tum, and coconut ice cream; approx. 150–250 THB

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is cash only — bring enough baht before boarding the longtail. The viewpoint hike involves rope climbing on steep sections — wear sturdy shoes. Longtail boats run until around 6–7 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Krabi to Koh Lanta by ferry or minivan-ferry combo (approx. 2–2.5 hours, 350–500 THB). Check into a mid-range bungalow resort on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — the most popular and beautiful beach on Koh Lanta. Settle in and enjoy the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (approx. 200–300 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta. Visit the charming Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a stilted fishing village with colorful wooden shophouses, art galleries, and a multicultural Muslim-Buddhist heritage. Browse local craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Ride to Kantiang Bay or Klong Nin Beach for a spectacular west-facing sunset. Watch the sun dip below the Andaman Sea horizon. Return to Long Beach for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light snack before departure from Krabi
meals.lunch: Old Town café — fresh seafood noodles or a local Muslim-style rice dish (khao mok gai); approx. 100–180 THB
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant on Long Beach — grilled whole fish, tom kha soup, and jasmine rice; approx. 250–400 THB

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is the best way to explore Koh Lanta — the island is 30 km long. Always wear a helmet. October can bring afternoon rain showers — carry a light poncho. Koh Lanta has a more relaxed, less commercialized vibe than Phi Phi.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island — explore jungle trails, visit the lighthouse with panoramic views, and spot wildlife including monitor lizards and tropical birds. Entry fee approx. 200 THB.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a snorkeling day trip from Koh Lanta to the pristine Koh Rok islands (approx. 1,200–1,500 THB) — renowned for some of the clearest water and best coral reefs in the Andaman Sea. Alternatively, relax on Bamboo Bay (a quiet, sheltered cove within the national park).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach. Enjoy a beachfront massage (Thai massage approx. 300–400 THB/hour). Watch the sunset with a cocktail from a beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local warung near Long Beach — roti canai with dhal curry (Muslim-style breakfast); approx. 60–100 THB
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included with Koh Rok snorkeling tour, or buy from a vendor near the national park
meals.dinner: Time for Lime Restaurant — a social enterprise restaurant on Koh Lanta offering Thai cooking classes and fresh cuisine; approx. 300–500 THB

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is a protected marine park with limited daily visitors — book the snorkeling trip early. The national park lighthouse trail is manageable but can be muddy after rain. Bring insect repellent for the jungle trails.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Thai cooking class on Koh Lanta (approx. 1,000–1,500 THB for a half-day class) — learn to make Southern Thai dishes like massaman curry, green papaya salad, and pad thai. Most classes include a market visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a leisurely afternoon on Klong Nin Beach — a quieter, more laid-back beach on the west coast with a bohemian vibe, beach bars, and excellent swimming. Rent a sunbed and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Long Beach for the evening. Browse the small night market near the beach road for souvenirs and street snacks. Enjoy a final relaxed evening on Koh Lanta.

meals.breakfast: Local Muslim bakery near Long Beach — fresh pastries, banana roti, and Thai iced coffee; approx. 80–120 THB
meals.lunch: Eat what you cooked during the cooking class — part of the class experience
meals.dinner: Klong Nin Beach restaurant — wood-fired pizza or fresh seafood BBQ; approx. 250–400 THB

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a highlight — book in advance as classes fill up quickly. Time for Lime and Lanta Thai Cookery School are both well-regarded. Pick up local spice pastes and souvenirs at the market during the class visit.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Koh Lanta by ferry back to Krabi, then connect to Phuket by minivan or bus (total travel approx. 3–4 hours). Check into a mid-range hotel in Patong Beach or Kata Beach area. Freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kata Beach or Karon Beach — both are beautiful, less hectic alternatives to Patong. Swim in the warm Andaman waters and enjoy the beach. Browse the local shops and beachfront cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Patong Beach for the famous Bangla Road night scene — a vibrant pedestrian street lined with bars, live music, street food, and entertainment. Experience the lively atmosphere (can be busy and loud — go with an open mind).

meals.breakfast: Light snack before departure from Koh Lanta
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant or food court during the journey — khao man gai (poached chicken rice); approx. 60–100 THB
meals.dinner: Patong street food stalls on Bangla Road — grilled seafood skewers, pad thai, and fresh fruit shakes; approx. 150–250 THB

day_by_day.notes: Kata Beach is quieter and more family-friendly than Patong — a good choice if you prefer a calmer base. The minivan/ferry combo from Koh Lanta to Phuket can be booked through your hotel or at the pier. Keep valuables secure in busy Patong.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Phuket Old Town — explore the beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese shophouses, colorful street art murals, and heritage buildings. Visit Thalang Road and Soi Rommanee for the best photo opportunities. Browse local antique shops and boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a speedboat tour to the famous Phang Nga Bay — visit James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), paddle a kayak through sea caves and mangrove tunnels, and marvel at the dramatic limestone karsts rising from the emerald water (approx. 1,500–2,000 THB for a full-day tour).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Phuket Old Town or a beachfront restaurant at Kata Beach.

meals.breakfast: Kopitiam by Wilai in Phuket Old Town — authentic Phuket-style breakfast with o-tao (oyster omelet), mee sua noodles, and local coffee; approx. 150–250 THB
meals.lunch: Lunch included in most Phang Nga Bay tours (typically served on a floating village or island)
meals.dinner: The Charm Dining Restaurant in Phuket Old Town — upscale Thai cuisine in a heritage shophouse setting; approx. 400–700 THB per dish

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay tours depart early (around 8 AM) — arrange pickup from your hotel. The sea kayaking through caves is a highlight — some caves require lying flat in the kayak during low tide. Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot in the morning before it gets hot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — depending on your departure time, enjoy a last swim at your chosen beach or revisit a favorite café in Phuket Old Town. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Phuket Weekend Market (Naka Market) if it's a weekend, or at the local night bazaar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Phuket International Airport for your departure. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for the journey and check-in. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, island hopping, and street food adventures across Thailand's Andaman Coast.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — khao tom (rice porridge) with crispy garlic and ginger, or a fresh fruit smoothie bowl from a beachside café; approx. 100–200 THB
meals.lunch: Airport food court or a quick meal near the hotel before departure; approx. 150–300 THB
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at your connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Pack any liquid souvenirs (fish sauce, coconut oil, curry pastes) in your checked luggage. Keep receipts for VAT refund claims at the airport (minimum purchase 2,000 THB per store). Exchange remaining Thai baht before departure or at the airport. Leave a review for your favorite guesthouses and tour operators to support local businesses!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and collect luggage. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer whisks you to the pier for a speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands. Enjoy the stunning Andaman Sea scenery on the 90-minute crossing. Check in to your boutique stay, unwind with a welcome drink, and settle into your villa.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Tonsai Bay's lively waterfront as the sun sets over the limestone karsts. Explore the local night bazaar for a taste of authentic Thai street snacks — grilled satay, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut ice cream.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-transit)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick premium airport meal at Suvarnabhumi's finest lounge or a riverside café near the pier before departure
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi — a beloved island institution serving refined Thai and Scandinavian fusion with fresh seafood in a relaxed open-air setting

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your private speedboat transfer in advance. October marks the tail end of the green season — expect lush scenery and occasional short showers. Pack a light rain jacket in your day bag.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise kayaking tour around the iconic Phi Phi Leh cliffs and Viking Cave. A private guided kayak experience through emerald lagoons and sea caves offers an intimate, crowd-free start to the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a premium longtail boat charter to Pileh Lagoon and Maya Bay (now managed with timed-entry permits). Snorkel the crystal-clear waters teeming with reef fish and vibrant coral. Return via Monkey Beach for a playful stop.
day_by_day.evening: Climb the Phi Phi Viewpoint at dusk for panoramic golden-hour views over both bays. Descend for cocktails at a clifftop bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at your boutique hotel — fresh tropical fruits, pastries, eggs to order, and freshly brewed Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ lunch on a private beach stop during your boat charter — grilled prawns, fish, and papaya salad prepared by your boat crew
meals.dinner: The Nest Restaurant at Zeavola Resort — an elegant jungle-garden setting with refined Thai cuisine, signature cocktails, and attentive service

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay requires advance booking of timed-entry slots. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a dry bag for valuables on the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga session on your villa terrace or the hotel's beachfront deck, followed by a relaxing Thai herbal steam and traditional massage at the hotel spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private speedboat to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) — a pristine, relatively uncrowded island with powdery white sand and turquoise shallows. Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkelling, and lounging in paradise.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don for a Thai cooking class with a private chef — learn to prepare pad kra pao, tom kha gai, and mango sticky rice using fresh market ingredients.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast in bed or on your private terrace — eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed juices, and tropical fruit platters
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper prepared by the hotel, enjoyed on Bamboo Island — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class as your meal, paired with Thai craft beers or a bottle of chilled Riesling

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least one day in advance through your hotel concierge. Bamboo Island is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend day-trippers.

day_by_day.morning: Morning freediving or scuba diving lesson/dive at Hin Daeng and Hin Muang — among Thailand's top dive sites, known for manta rays, leopard sharks, and spectacular soft coral walls. Depart early by private speedboat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Surface interval and light lunch on the boat, then a second dive or snorkel at Koh Haa — a cluster of five limestone islands with exceptional underwater visibility and diverse marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi by late afternoon. Freshen up and head out for a fire show on the beach — a quintessential Phi Phi evening experience — followed by a leisurely walk through the night market.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — granola, yoghurt, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh onboard lunch prepared by your dive charter crew — Thai rice dishes, grilled fish, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant, Phi Phi — a long-standing favourite for authentic, flavour-forward Thai dishes including massaman curry, green curry, and fresh whole fish

day_by_day.notes: Hin Daeng and Hin Muang are approximately 2–2.5 hours by speedboat from Phi Phi. Book a reputable PADI-certified dive operator. Non-divers can snorkel at Koh Haa instead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at leisure — swim off your hotel's private beach, read on a sun lounger, or indulge in a 90-minute traditional Thai oil massage at the spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Don's quieter northern bays — Laem Tong Beach and Nui Beach — areas less visited by day-trippers. Swim, snorkel, and explore hidden coves at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail cruise around Phi Phi Leh on a chartered traditional wooden boat, watching the limestone towers glow amber and pink at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast with made-to-order omelets, smoked salmon, fresh juices, and Thai congee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Laem Tong — fresh seafood grilled on the spot by local fishermen, served with sticky rice and spicy dipping sauces
meals.dinner: In-villa private dining experience arranged by your hotel — a curated five-course Thai tasting menu with wine pairing, served under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The private villa dining experience should be arranged 24 hours in advance with the hotel concierge. Sunset cocktail cruises typically depart around 17:00–17:30.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands by private speedboat transfer to Krabi Town. Check in to a luxury property such as Rayavadee or Phulay Bay, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve in Railay/Krabi area. Freshen up and explore the hotel grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private longtail boat to Railay Beach — one of Thailand's most dramatic and beautiful beaches, accessible only by boat. Explore Railay West, Railay East, and the hidden Phra Nang Cave Beach with its royal spirit shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a beachside bar on Railay West, watching the sun dip behind the karst formations. Return to your hotel for a refined evening.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at your Phi Phi boutique stay before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Railay Beach — The Grotto at Rayavadee (if staying there) or a premium beachside restaurant serving fresh Thai seafood
meals.dinner: Krabi's finest fine dining — Sala Krabi or the Ritz-Carlton's signature restaurant — featuring contemporary Thai cuisine with locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your private speedboat transfer from Phi Phi to Krabi the day before. Railay is a 15-minute longtail ride from Ao Nang or Krabi Town pier.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning rock climbing lesson on Railay's famous limestone cliffs with a certified private guide — suitable for beginners and offering breathtaking views from the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Four Islands boat tour — visit Koh Poda, Koh Gai (Chicken Island), Koh Tub, and Koh Mor. Snorkel the coral gardens, walk the sandbar between islands at low tide, and relax on pristine beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town for a street food evening walk — explore the Krabi Walking Street Night Market (open Fridays and Saturdays) for local delicacies: roti with banana and Nutella, pad thai, grilled seafood, and fresh fruit shakes.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — a lavish spread of local and international options
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on Koh Poda island — your private charter includes a gourmet packed lunch with fresh salads, sandwiches, and tropical fruits
meals.dinner: Krabi Walking Street Night Market street food feast, followed by a nightcap cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Krabi River

day_by_day.notes: The walking street night market operates on Fridays and Saturdays. If visiting on another day, Viva Restaurant or Carnivore Steak & Grill in Krabi Town are excellent premium alternatives.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for a panoramic 360-degree view over Krabi's jungle and karst landscape. An exhilarating and spiritual start to the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through the mangrove forests of Ao Thalane — a UNESCO-recommended site with serene waterways, rich birdlife, and dramatic cliff backdrops. Private guided half-day tour.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the hotel spa — a signature Thai herbal compress massage and aromatherapy facial. Dinner at leisure at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the temple climb — fresh fruit, yoghurt, and coffee at the hotel
meals.lunch: Post-kayak lunch at a riverside restaurant in Ao Thalane — fresh grilled fish, tom yum soup, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant dinner — order the chef's signature tasting menu featuring southern Thai specialities: massaman lamb, crab curry, and pandan desserts

day_by_day.notes: Start the Tiger Cave Temple climb before 08:00 to avoid heat and crowds. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The mangrove kayak tour is best at high tide — confirm timing with your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip by private speedboat to the Trang Islands — depart early for Koh Kradan, consistently rated one of Thailand's most beautiful and least-crowded islands. Snorkel the pristine reef directly from the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping to Koh Mook and the magical Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot) — swim through a 80-metre dark sea cave to emerge in a hidden inland beach surrounded by towering jungle walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi by speedboat. Sunset drinks on your hotel terrace or poolside, followed by a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — eggs to order, toast, fresh juices, and Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch on Koh Kradan — fresh seafood BBQ with a cold Chang beer under the shade of palm trees
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at Mangrove Restaurant, Krabi — celebrated for its fresh catch, authentic southern Thai recipes, and romantic riverside ambience

day_by_day.notes: The Trang Islands are approximately 1.5–2 hours from Krabi by speedboat. Emerald Cave must be visited at low tide and requires swimming in the dark — bring a waterproof torch. Book this excursion through a reputable operator.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer from Krabi to Koh Lanta by private speedboat (approx. 1.5 hours). Check in to a luxury villa resort such as Pimalai Resort & Spa or Sri Lanta Resort. Enjoy a welcome ceremony and explore the property.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Old Town of Koh Lanta (Ban Ko Lanta) — a historic Sino-Portuguese fishing village with wooden shophouses, art galleries, and local craft shops. Stroll the atmospheric pier and interact with the local sea gypsy community.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Long Beach (Klong Dao) — one of Koh Lanta's finest stretches of sand. Enjoy cocktails at a beachfront bar as the sky turns crimson over the Andaman.

meals.breakfast: Final Krabi hotel breakfast before transfer
meals.lunch: Lunch in Koh Lanta Old Town — a family-run restaurant serving traditional Malay-influenced Thai dishes: fish curry, roti, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Pimalai's Spice & Rice restaurant (or equivalent resort restaurant) — elevated Thai cuisine in an open-air pavilion overlooking the sea, with an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta Old Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. Ask your hotel concierge to arrange bicycle rentals for the afternoon. October is low season on Koh Lanta — expect fewer crowds and lush, green scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private speedboat charter around Koh Lanta Marine National Park — visit the stunning Koh Rok islands (twin islands with crystal-clear waters and vibrant coral reefs, considered some of Thailand's best snorkelling spots).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Koh Ha for a second snorkel stop before a leisurely return to Koh Lanta. Relax on the boat's sun deck with chilled beverages as the islands drift by.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront bonfire dinner arranged by your resort — a romantic private setup with a personal chef preparing a fresh seafood feast: whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, scallops, and Thai salads.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — tropical buffet with freshly baked pastries, eggs station, and a smoothie bar
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard lunch on the charter boat — Thai rice boxes, fresh fruit, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Private beachfront bonfire dinner — a bespoke luxury experience arranged through the hotel concierge

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is protected marine park — reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory. Book the private bonfire dinner at least 48 hours in advance. Koh Rok is approximately 1 hour from Koh Lanta by speedboat.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — final swim in the Andaman Sea, a poolside breakfast, and a long farewell massage at the resort spa. Savour the last moments of island tranquillity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta's jungle interior on a private ATV or bicycle tour — visit a rubber plantation, a local elephant sanctuary (ethical, no-riding), and a hidden waterfall. A wonderful contrast to the beach days.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on Koh Lanta — cocktails at a rooftop bar watching the last sunset of the trip, followed by a street food exploration of the local market for one final taste of Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte breakfast at the resort — avocado toast, açaí bowls, and freshly brewed single-origin Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Local Thai restaurant near the elephant sanctuary — simple, authentic, and delicious home-style cooking
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Where Else? Restaurant, Koh Lanta — a beloved beachside venue with superb fresh fish, creative cocktails, and a warm, convivial atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your ethical elephant sanctuary visit in advance — look for sanctuaries that prioritise elephant welfare with no riding or performances. Pack your bags this evening for an early departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning farewell breakfast at the resort. Private speedboat or ferry transfer from Koh Lanta to Krabi Airport (allow 2.5–3 hours including transfer and check-in time). Depart Thailand with extraordinary memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure flight from Krabi or onward travel. If time permits before the flight, browse Krabi Airport's duty-free for Thai silk, artisan crafts, and premium Thai tea and coffee to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or onward journey

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — make it special with champagne, fresh tropical fruits, and your favourite Thai dishes one last time
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining at Krabi International Airport or onboard meal
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at your next destination

day_by_day.notes: Krabi Airport is approximately 45 minutes from the Krabi pier and 2+ hours from Koh Lanta including the ferry. Plan your departure carefully and always build in extra buffer time. Ensure all souvenirs, including any Thai food products, comply with customs regulations for your home country.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
